hero.filename: Sukhothai, Wat Traphang Ngoen, Lake, Thailand.jpg
hero.caption: Beautiful Wat Traphang Ngoen on the lake. Wat Traphang Ngoen means "silver lake monastery". The temple was probably built in the 14th century, at the same time with Wat Mahathat. Wat Traphang Ngoen is oriented so that it is illuminated by both rising and setting sun. Sukhothai, Thailand.

images.filename: Inscription Stele of King Ramkamhaeng the Great. Bangkok National Museum b072.jpg
images.caption: This stele bears a written date of 1292. It displays a biography of Ramkamhaeng that is traditionally, but controversially, attributed to the King himself. It is one of the very few sources of information that we have about this semilegendary monarch.

images.caption: Sukhothai ponds are full of lotus flowers. In Buddhist symbolism, the lotus represents purity of the body, speech and mind, as if floating above the murky waters of material attachment and physical desire. In Tantric and Yogic traditions it symbolizes the realization of inner potential to harness the flow of energy moving through the chakras. Sukhothai, Thailand.
